newsitem.title: CHINA: China to expand local currency interbank market.
newsitem.headline: China to expand local currency interbank market.

text.p: China will expand its local currency interbank market in 1997 by allowing branches of major commercial banks and city cooperative banks to trade directly on the market, a senior exchange official said.

"The central government is considering allowing branches of major banks and hundreds of city cooperative banks to participate in the first tier of trading on the market," Pang Jiying, deputy president of the China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS), said on Wednesday.
"It is also considering how to allow foreign banks to participate in the interbank market after approving them to do local currency business," Pang told a seminar in Shanghai.
Growth of the Chinese yuan interbank market, which allows banks to swap short-term funds amongst themselves, is seen as one of the key building blocks of the reform of China's financial system.
Since the market was established in January 1996, it has operated in a limited and experimental way with the authorities refusing to say when its operations will be formalised.

The market currently has 55 first tier members -- 20 major Chinese bank head offices and 35 short-term financial centres, which are the money brokerages run by the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
Foreign banks, minor Chinese banks, securities houses and other financial institutions can build or clear positions through the members, and their trades are called secondary market trading.
Pang said the market was still too small, with rates on the secondary market differing from one part of the country to another, making them an inaccurate reflection of short-term money movements.
"The central bank has said that it will expand the market this year," Pang said.
"It has expressed the intention to combine the foreign exchange and local currency interbank markets to make them into a unified market called the China National Interbank Lending Centre," he said.
The yuan interbank market traded a total of 58.72 billion yuan ($7.07 billion) in its first year of operations last year, only a fraction of the volume on China's state debt and stock markets.
Pang said the establishment of a unified market must be gradual and required careful management and strict risk control.
Once a unified market supported by unified quotations and rules is established, the goal of the market -- achieving effective money movements -- will be reached, he said.
"With the expansion of the market, the central government is also studying how to trade short-term bills issued by the central bank and state debt," Pang said.
The yuan market currently trades seven contracts of one day, seven, 20, 30, 60, 90 and 120 days duration. Pang said this range would be gradually expanded to allow more contracts over the next year.
Interbank market traders welcomed the news of an expansion of the interbank market's first tier membership.

"The expansion of the market is healthy, but there are still many other problems to be solved, including the limitations on trading volumes placed on members by the central bank, and several technical problems," one trader said.
